outcomes.text: Explain how texts are made in and for different contexts.
Analyse language choices for purposes and contexts using terms like personification, voice-over and flashback.
Judge how mode and medium, including digital, shape audience response.

subtopics.title: Features and conventions of text types

outcomes.text: Explain how language features, structures and conventions convey ideas and viewpoints.
Explain how structures, features and style choices work in different text types.
Analyse how vocabulary, idiom and rhetoric serve different purposes and contexts.
Evaluate the impact of description, imagery and figurative language, including still and moving images.
Analyse how a text's purpose, often debatable, influences responses.
Analyse how personal, social and cultural context influences responses.
Analyse how imaginative, persuasive and interpretive techniques influence responses.
Choose form, content, style and tone to suit purpose and audience in real and imagined contexts.
Use a range of technologies to research, communicate and represent ideas.
Combine visual, spoken and written elements where suitable.
Build evidence-based arguments.
Quote and reference sources properly.
Plan, draft, edit and proofread.
Use accurate spelling, punctuation, syntax and metalanguage.

subtopics.title: Reflecting on own and others' texts

outcomes.text: Use textual evidence to assess the purpose and context of texts.
Question responses to texts.
Investigate the impact and uses of imaginative, interpretive and persuasive texts.

subtopics.title: Comparing purpose, style and hybrid texts

outcomes.text: Explain the relationship between purpose and context.
Analyse the style and structure of texts, including digital ones.
Evaluate similarities and differences between hybrid texts such as infotainment and hypertext fiction.

topics.title: Representation of ideas, attitudes and voices

outcomes.text: Analyse how features, structures and style shape viewpoints and influence audiences.
Evaluate rhetorical devices like emphasis, emotive language and imagery in argument.
Analyse effects of multimodal and digital conventions such as navigation, sound and image.
Analyse how attitude and mood arise, for example through humour in satire and parody.
Evaluate how language and structure choices shape own and others' perspectives.
Examine how ideas and voices are represented, such as differing media reports of events.
Analyse how imaginative, persuasive and interpretive techniques interplay, as with anecdotes in speeches.
Analyse how responses change over time and across cultures.
Use imaginative, interpretive and persuasive elements for different purposes and audiences.
Experiment with structures, language features and multimodal devices.
Develop and keep a consistent voice, tone and style.
Choose and apply textual evidence to support arguments.
Plan, draft, edit and proofread.
Use accurate spelling, punctuation, syntax and metalanguage.
Analyse values and attitudes expressed in texts.
Evaluate how well texts represent ideas, attitudes and voices.
Explain how and why texts position readers and viewers.
Analyse language, structure and style choices when comparing texts.
Explain how texts follow or challenge genre or mode conventions, for example crime fiction or advertising.
Compare how similar themes and ideas are treated in different texts.
Analyse techniques and conventions across genres, mediums and modes.
Consider how genre conventions can be challenged, manipulated or parodied.
Examine how genres and conventions change over time.
Analyse how language patterns create shades of meaning.
Analyse how genre expectations develop and what happens when they are met, extended or subverted.
Analyse how responses to genres change over time and across cultures.
Transform and adapt texts for different purposes, contexts and audiences.
Use language features in innovative, imaginative ways.
Experiment with genre-specific structures and features for effect.
Sustain analysis and argument.
Reference with footnotes, in-line citations and reference lists.
Plan, draft, edit and proofread.
Use accurate spelling, punctuation, syntax and metalanguage.
Evaluate how different texts represent similar ideas differently.
Explain how meaning changes when a text moves to another genre or medium.
Compare and evaluate the impact of language conventions across texts and genres.
Closely analyse texts.
Examine how each text relates to its context or contexts.
Compare the contexts in which texts are created and received.
Analyse content, purpose and language choices.
Analyse voice and point of view in feature articles, news reports or narration.
Explore other interpretations and context to build a considered response.
Evaluate how choice of mode, medium, genre and text type conveys perspective.
Evaluate how points of view and values are represented.
Evaluate language features that generate empathy or controversy, such as juxtaposing image and text.
Use language and style to sustain a personal voice and viewpoint.
Use nuanced language.
Synthesise ideas and opinions into a complex argument.
Justify own responses with textual evidence.
Reference with footnotes, in-line citations and reference lists.
Plan, draft, edit and proofread.
Use accurate spelling, punctuation, syntax and metalanguage.
Analyse how differing attitudes and perspectives underpin texts.
Question assumptions and values in texts.
Identify omissions, inclusions, emphases and marginalisations.
Discuss and evaluate different readings of texts.
